analysis.investment_thesis: Mastek is a compounding IT services machine — 23.3% revenue CAGR and 32.5% net profit CAGR over 9 years, now trading at a bargain 12.8x P/E. However, heavy dependence on UK government/public-sector contracts and a promoter stake of only 35.77% make this a cautious hold rather than a conviction buy for an investor seeking pure India-growth champions.
key_strengths: Exceptional 9-year compounding: Net profit CAGR 32.5%, FCF surged to ₹515 Cr in FY26 — true cash-generating business
Bargain valuation: 12.8x P/E and 9.8x EV/EBITDA for a proven double-digit compounder is deeply undervalued on any growth-adjusted metric
Asset-light, low-debt balance sheet: D/E of only 0.20, borrowings declining from ₹583 Cr to ₹438 Cr, OCF positive all 5 years
key_risks: UK/government concentration: Majority revenue from UK public sector — exactly the 'government contract dependency' red flag I always warn about, highly exposed to political and budget cycle risk
Low promoter holding at 35.77% — well below my 50% threshold; limited skin in the game raises long-term alignment concerns
Revenue growth decelerating: From ₹2,184 Cr (FY22) → ₹3,699 Cr (FY26) looks strong but sequential growth is flattening; not the accelerating story I seek
red_flags: Promoter stake at 35.77% — dangerously low; I need promoters who own the business, not just manage it
Finance costs exploded from ₹4 Cr (FY20) to ₹44 Cr (FY24) post-acquisition; FY23 investing outflow of ₹719 Cr signals an aggressive acquisition that temporarily crushed OCF to just ₹108 Cr
Not an India domestic story — this is a UK-facing IT services play; it does not ride India's consumption, urbanisation, or digital boom the way I prefer
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Mastek's numbers are genuinely impressive — a 9-year revenue CAGR of 23.3% with operating leverage delivering 33% EBIT CAGR is rare discipline. The FY26 FCF of ₹515 Cr against a market cap of ₹5,412 Cr implies a ~9.5% free cash flow yield, which is extraordinarily cheap. D/E at 0.20, ROCE at 18%, and 5-for-5 OCF positivity reflect clean financial management. At 12.8x P/E with an 11.29x forward P/E, the market is pricing in near-zero growth — that creates a margin of safety even for a skeptic.

The problem is the strategic DNA. Mastek derives the bulk of its revenue from UK government and public sector clients — precisely the kind of single-geography, government-contract dependency that can turn a profitable business into a painful one when Whitehall tightens budgets. The FY23 ₹719 Cr acquisition (likely Majesco-related integration or another bolt-on) disrupted cash flows and raised debt sharply. Most importantly, a promoter at 35.77% is a structural concern for me — great Indian businesses are built by promoters who own 55–70% and think in decades. The valuation compensates for some of this, but I cannot make it a high-conviction bet without seeing promoter holding rise and domestic India revenue contribution grow meaningfully.
